kjv: And I John saw the holy city
mine: And I saw the holy city
note: The TR adds egō Iōannēs "I John"; SBLGNT has only eidon "I saw".

kjv: a great voice out of heaven
mine: a loud voice from the throne
note: SBLGNT reads ek tou thronou "from the throne"; the TR reads ek tou ouranou "from heaven".

kjv: God himself shall be with them (human beings), and be their God
mine: God Himself will be with them (human beings)
note: The TR adds theos autōn "their God" at the end; SBLGNT lacks it.

kjv: they (human beings) shall be his (God's) people
mine: they (human beings) will be His (God's) peoples
note: Both Greek texts have the plural laoi "peoples". It recasts the covenant formula of Lev 26:12 to include many nations, and the KJV's singular loses that.
SBLGNT reads tauta "these things", the blessings just described; the TR reads panta "all things".

kjv: that great city, the holy Jerusalem
note: The TR reads tēn polin tēn megalēn tēn hagian "the great city, the holy", while SBLGNT has only tēn polin tēn hagian "the holy city". Without "great" the city is not echoing "the great city" Babylon.

kjv: the nations of them which are saved shall walk in the light of it (the city)
mine: The nations will walk by its (the city's) light
note: The TR adds tōn sōzomenōn "of those being saved", which narrows "the nations". SBLGNT says simply that the nations will walk by its light. The TR also adds kai tēn timēn "and honour" later in the verse.
SBLGNT reads pan koinon "anything unclean"; the TR reads pan koinoun "anything that defiles", an active participle.
